newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Record French, German stocks lead Europe up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Record French, German stocks lead Europe up.

text.p: European stock markets ended higher on Thursday, with the French and German bourses leading the way with record closes.

On the foreign exchange market, the dollar quietly held firm against the mark but eased to the day's low versus the yen. Sterling rose to its highest level since July 1992, bolstered by expectations of a British rate rise.

The dollar fell sharply against the Canadian dollar after the Bank of Canada raised its key Bank Rate 25 basis points to 3.5 percent, effectively raising the overnight lending rate's target range to between 3.0 and 3.5 percent.
In stocks, France's blue-chip CAC-40 stock index jumped about one percent with help from a turnaround in the Dow Jones Industrial Average into positive ground in the afternoon.

A near 20 percent surge in Rhone-Poulenc to close at 252.5 francs provided the French index with its initial boost early in the day. The chemical and drugs firm said it planned to buy out the rest of U.S. subsidiary Rhone Poulenc Rorer.
Turnover was heavy in the 40 constituent stocks of the CAC, estimated at 8.3 billion francs ($1.4 billion).
Germany's DAX index broke a psychological barrier at 3,800 to score a record high of 3,827.52 in early trade.
Profit-taking emerged in the late morning to knock the DAX off its peak, but it still managed to close at a record.

Traders said German shares were expected to remain buoyant in coming sessions as sector-rotations kept money in the market. Car shares looked to be the new favourites after brokers such as Merrill Lynch reiterated a strong buy recommendation for Volkswagen AG.
London's FTSE-100 index overcame opening weakness to finish higher for the third consecutive day.

Help came from oil stocks, which gained in line with firmer crude prices after the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) agreed to commit themselves to quotas and cut production until the end of the year.
"If you believe that, then oil prices look good for now and will continue to look good to the end of the year," said one dealer in the oil sector.
As the FTSE's rally took hold, worries faded over the Labour government's first budget on July 2 and the next monetary meeting on July 10.

The Labour government has promised to introduce a windfall tax on privatised utilities in the budget. But hopes that it would be smaller than previously expected boosted utility shares. National Power and PowerGen were among the sector's leaders.

London dealers saw signs that fund managers were scrambling to buy outperforming stocks before the first half ends next week so they can mark their portfolios up for end of the quarter results. This type of buying could keep shares lifted before the earnings onslaught begins.
U.S. technology stocks were already suffering after several companies issued warnings on earnings earlier.
CURRENCIES AT 1550 GMT
The dollar was at 113.22 yen and 1.7265 marks in late Europe, compared with 114.03 yen and 1.7243 marks in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 17.9 points at 4,657.90.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended up 26.20 points at 2,893.64.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 6.78 points at 3,805.29.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $338.15 an ounce against $338.25 at Wednesday's close. ($ = 5.822 French Francs)
